task.description: WF-03 Step 2 (fix design) for ISS-0765. Design the correction of web/src/api/identity.ts's groupsApi against the real, runtime-verified backend route table, including the .members response-shape mismatch that a prefix-only fix would unmask. Design only -- interfaces, exact type shapes, exact before/after URL literals, and the test matrix. NO implementation code.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: groupsApi's .addMembers/.list/.get/.update/.delete/.members each call a URL prefix a real backend route serves, audited against the actual route table rather than assumed
AC2: each corrected call has regression coverage mirroring web/src/api/__tests__/identity.removeMembers.test.ts

AC3: npm run type-check and the web test suite pass, and any groupsApi call with no corresponding backend route is either removed or explicitly recorded as unimplemented rather than left pointing at a dead prefix
Four named design decisions (a-d) each stated as a decision with justification, not as a list of options
Scope boundary held: groupsApi only; usersApi/rolesApi (ISS-0812), Group.is_system/member_count (ISS-0811) and the generic coupling guard (ISS-0813) untouched

a_get_and_update.decision: DELETE both groupsApi.get and groupsApi.update, and leave a comment block in their place recording that GET /groups/:id and PATCH|PUT /groups/:id are unimplemented backend-side.
a_get_and_update.justification: No route exists at any prefix and no Letflow.Identity get_group/update_group context function exists, so a prefix 'correction' only moves the 404 from ApiPipeline's catch-all (api_pipeline.ex:203-205) to Letflow.Routers.Identity's own match _ (identity.ex:227). Zero production callers. Adding the routes is new backend behaviour = WF-01, out of scope. AC3 permits removal; deletion PLUS the recorded comment satisfies both halves of AC3's disjunction and is what stops a fourth run re-adding them.
a_get_and_update.consequence_recorded: ISS-0765's own fix_direction ('correct .get/.update to the real prefix') is NOT satisfiable as written. The design says so explicitly in §2 so Step 5 does not close the issue claiming a correction that was not made.

b_members_shape.decision: RETYPE. groupsApi.members(id) returns Promise<GroupMemberPage> = { items: GroupMember[]; next_cursor: string | null; count: number } -- the backend envelope verbatim. The API client performs NO unwrapping. GroupsPage.tsx reads .items.
b_members_shape.justification: docs/guides/frontend_developer_guide.md §4 rule 1 forbids the alternative outright ('Do not add a shim or adapter inside web/ that normalises the mismatch'), so this is a recorded project rule rather than a preference. Second: the retype makes tsc the detector for the run's highest-risk item -- any call site still treating the value as an array becomes a type error, so `npm run type-check` (AC3) mechanically finds every one, whereas an unwrap would let type-check pass whether or not the shape was ever considered. Third: an unwrap discards next_cursor and hides that the route is cursor-paginated.
b_members_shape.exact_type: GroupMemberPage { items: GroupMember[]; next_cursor: string | null; count: number }; GroupMember { id: string; username: string; display_name: string; email: string; status: 'active' | 'inactive'; auth_source: 'internal' | 'oidc'; inserted_at: string; updated_at: string } -- user_map/1 (lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex:729-740) transcribed exactly.
groupspage_lines_changed: new line after :58 -- `const members = useMemo(() => membersPage?.items ?? [], [membersPage?.items])`
b_members_shape.fail_first_evidence: REWORK 1: the M-1a/M-1b type-check mutants in design section 7.1, NOT any runtime row. No vitest row can discriminate a TypeScript return-type change, because client.ts passes the body through verbatim and T is erased at runtime.

c_addmembers.decision: RENAME to addMember(id: string, userId: string), body { user_id: userId }, return type GroupMemberAddResult { group_id: string; user_id: string; created: boolean }. Sole caller GroupsPage.tsx:76 becomes groupsApi.addMember(id, userId).
c_addmembers.justification: resolve_member_user_id/1 (lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex:525-537) matches %{"user_ids" => [first | _rest]} and returns only `first`; the comment at identity.ex:483-489 records this as a deliberate R-Co port decision, so under core-directives' 'Don't silently re-decide what a decision record already settled' the client is the side that must move. Its FIRST clause matches %{"user_id" => user_id}, so singular is the backend's primary shape. It mirrors the ISS-0736 removeMembers correction exactly -- the identical defect in the adjacent function. Against the scope boundary: groupsApi and its directly-consequent GroupsPage call sites are explicitly in scope, and the sole caller already passes [userId], a one-element array literal, so the change removes a wrapper and alters no behaviour.
c_addmembers.stale_premise_note: REWORK 1, folded in from the gate: the routers/identity.ex:483-489 comment's own premise ("no existing Letflow caller depends on the array shape either way") is stale today, because GroupsPage.tsx:76 passes [userId]. Decision (c) does not contradict the recorded backend decision -- it restores that premise by removing the one caller that had drifted from it. Recorded in design section 4 so a later reader does not re-litigate it.

d_list_type.decision: CORRECT IT NOW. groupsApi.list() returns Promise<GroupListResponse> where GroupListResponse = { items: Group[]; total: number }. PagedResponse<T> itself is NOT modified.
d_list_type.justification: handle_list_groups/2 (identity.ex:468-472) emits only items+total; PagedResponse<T> declares page and page_size as REQUIRED, so the type is false today and a future data.page_size read gets undefined with no type error -- the same silent-wrong-value class this run exists to remove. Verified zero call-site cost: all three consumers (GroupsPage.tsx:50, UserDetailPage.tsx:149, useAdminUsers.ts:47) read .items only and .total is read nowhere. PagedResponse<T> stays untouched because usersApi/rolesApi also use it and are out of scope (ISS-0812).

test_matrix.mirrors: web/src/api/__tests__/identity.removeMembers.test.ts -- // @vitest-environment jsdom, a window.fetch spy assigned from vi.fn(), setToken/clearToken in beforeEach/afterEach, assertions on the exact method + path requested
test_matrix.guard_constraint: web/tests/guards/source-scan.spec.ts scans web/src/**/*.{ts,tsx} INCLUDING __tests__/, and forbidlist.ts's raw-fetch-outside-client pattern (/\bfetch\(|\baxios\(/) allows only web/src/api/client.ts. Assign the spy (window.fetch = fetchSpy as unknown as typeof window.fetch); never write the literal text 'fetch('. Weakening the pattern is forbidden (INV-F).

rows.assertion: list() -> GET, URL contains /api/v1/identity/groups and NOT /api/v1/admin/groups
create({name,display_name,description}) -> POST /api/v1/identity/groups; parsed body deep-equals the passed object
that request's parsed body deep-equals { user_id: 'u-1' } and 'user_ids' in body === false
typeof groupsApi.addMember === 'function', addMember.length === 2, 'addMembers' in groupsApi === false

ONE it block, both halves together. (i) path half: members('g-1') -> GET, captured URL contains /api/v1/identity/groups/g-1/members and NOT /api/v1/admin/. (ii) no-unwrap half: with the spy resolving {"items":[<one user_map object>],"next_cursor":null,"count":1}, the awaited value deep-equals it -- result.items.length === 1, result.count === 1, result.next_cursor === null, Array.isArray(result) === false. REWORK 1: merged from the former rows 7 and 8 so the block contains an assertion that can actually be red.
rows.pre_fix: FAILS on half (i) only -- the pre-fix literal is /api/v1/admin/groups/${id}/members. Half (ii) PASSES pre-fix and post-fix alike (see section 7.1); it is a forward regression guard against a future .items unwrap, NOT fail-first evidence.

rows.assertion: 'get' in groupsApi === false AND 'update' in groupsApi === false
it.each over all six surviving functions: invoke each, assert no captured URL contains /api/v1/admin/ -- one row per function so a failure names the function

rows.pre_fix: PASSES -- enumeration row, NOT fail-first evidence; its job is to prove this run did not regress the ISS-0736 correction while rewriting the object around it.

test_matrix.members_consumer_coverage: Covered by `npm run type-check`, deliberately, not by a render test -- and M-1a is the recorded proof that the detector actually fires. After the retype, any call site treating GroupMemberPage as an array is a compile error, so tsc -b tsconfig.json (AC3, already inside npm run check) finds every one on every run. No GroupsPage component test exists to extend and adding the project's first one is UI-test scope this run does not carry. This is a decision, not an omitted test.

fail_first_accounting.why_no_runtime_row_can_cover_the_retype: request<T> (web/src/api/client.ts:158-169) ends in `return response.json() as Promise<T>` -- a verbatim pass-through -- and T is a TypeScript type parameter erased at runtime. Pre-fix client.get<User[]> and post-fix client.get<GroupMemberPage> therefore produce byte-identical runtime behaviour on the same spy body. Claiming a runtime row covers decision (b) is a design error, which is what the gate caught.

mutants.rationale: WF-03 Step 4's clause for "when the pre-fix failure is non-existence" applied by analogy: a type-only change has no runtime failure to demonstrate, so the fail-first requirement is met by mutating the shipped change and recording what breaks. Specified here by design rather than left to TEST-DESIGNER.

M-1a.what: On the post-fix tree, keep section 3.1 GroupMemberPage/GroupMember and the retyped groupsApi.members; revert ONLY section 3.2's six GroupsPage.tsx edits to their pre-fix text.
M-1a.expected: tsc errors on GroupsPage.tsx at the reverted :103, :223, :227, :228 -- .map/.length do not exist on GroupMemberPage, user_id does not exist on GroupMember. Quote verbatim.
M-1a.and_also: npm test still PASSES under M-1a. That is the point: it demonstrates the runtime suite is blind to the retype while type-check is not.

M-1b.what: The opposite-direction control: revert section 3.1's retype to client.get<User[]> while keeping section 3.2's GroupsPage.tsx edits.
M-1b.expected: tsc errors on membersPage?.items over User[]. Recording both directions is what shows the probe discriminates the specific trap rather than merely breaking something.

mutants.revert_discipline: Binding, per WF-03 Step 4's mutant rule. Apply in a throwaway git worktree of the branch, or in place then `git checkout -- <path>`; either way, before completing the handoff, quote BOTH (a) `git status --porcelain web/` empty and (b) `npm run type-check` and `npm test` green against the restored tree.

acceptance_criteria_map.AC1: §1.1 mount chain + §1.2 six-route list, both re-derived from source in this step; §1.4 per-function verdicts; §6.1 exact before/after URL literals. .get/.update satisfied by §2's removal (no served prefix exists); the other four by the §6.1 substitutions. Tests: rows 1-5, 7(i), 10.
acceptance_criteria_map.AC2: Section 7: one row per corrected call -- list (1), create (2), delete (3), addMember (4,5,6), members (7) -- in a new file reusing the ISS-0736 file's jsdom + window.fetch-spy structure, plus the table-driven class guard (10) and the untouched-removeMembers row (11). Section 7.1's M-1a/M-1b mutants supply the fail-first evidence for the .members retype, which no runtime row can.
acceptance_criteria_map.AC3: §2 removes .get/.update AND leaves the recorded rationale comment (both halves of AC3's disjunction). §3's retype is what makes type-check a real detector rather than a formality; §5 removes the second type lie. §7 names the three commands whose actual output Step 4 must quote. Tests: rows 8, 9, plus section 7.1's M-1a -- the recorded proof that type-check actually fires on a missed .members consumer.

invariants: INV-A: every post-fix groupsApi URL literal resolves to one of the six routes in §1.2; no groupsApi literal contains /api/v1/admin/
INV-B: every declared return type in groupsApi is the wire body of its route -- no shim, no unwrap, no reshaping inside web/src/api/ (frontend_developer_guide.md §4 rule 1)
INV-C: groupsApi.removeMembers and identity.removeMembers.test.ts are byte-unchanged
INV-D: usersApi, rolesApi, tokensApi, PagedResponse<T>, CursorPage<T>, User and Group are unmodified; only additive interfaces are added to web/src/types/api.ts
INV-E: no file under lib/, priv/repo/migrations/ or test/ is modified
INV-F: no forbidlist.ts entry is weakened, removed or allowedPaths-exempted for the new test file
open_questions: OQ-1 (RESOLVED BY THE GATE, rework 1, in CODE-DESIGNER's favour): the scope boundary's two clauses overlap on Group -- "member/Group TS types that misdescribe the wire shape" is IN scope while is_system/member_count is OUT (ISS-0811), and Group.is_system is in both sets. CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR confirmed the ISS-0811 carve-out wins: Group stays untouched, GroupMember is new and additive, GroupListResponse changes only the envelope. No rework to section 3.1 or section 5 on that ground. The OQ is retained in the design as the record of how the overlap was resolved and by whom.

OQ-2: GroupMemberPage.next_cursor is typed and returned but never read -- the members dialog is capped at the first 50 (Pagination.default_page_size/0). Whether to page the dialog or send page_size=200 has no acceptance criterion in this run and is reported to ORCH rather than settled. FRONTEND-DEV must NOT add a page_size query param on its own initiative.
summary.verification_note: No implementation code was written, in the original pass or in rework 1. `git status --porcelain web/ lib/letflow/routers/ lib/letflow/identity* test/ priv/` is empty; the only files this step touches are the design artefact under lib/letflow/design/ and this handoff.
summary.rework_1_note: Two gate findings, both accepted in full and both fixed in this pass: F-1 (BLOCKING -- the T-0765-MEMBERS-SHAPE row could not fail pre-fix, and the section summary claiming rows 1-11 all failed was false) and F-2 (ambiguous bare identity.ex citations). Neither touched a decision: (a)-(d) all stand, and sections 1-6, 8 and 9 survived the validator's independent re-derivation unchanged.

issues.description: FACTUAL ERROR IN THE STEP 1 DIAGNOSIS, corrected here by re-derivation. step-01-issue-fixer.json's blast_radius.consumers_of_useAdminGroups says 'No consumer of useAdminGroups was found outside web/src/hooks/useAdminUsers.ts itself' and asked CODE-DESIGNER to re-verify. It is false: web/src/pages/admin/UserDetailPage.tsx:28 calls useAdminGroups() and reads groupsQuery.data?.items at :149. groupsApi.list has THREE consumers, not two. All three read .items only, so decision (d) still costs zero call-site changes -- but that is now a measured fact rather than an inherited one. No separate issue needed if ORCH notes it on ISS-0765.

NEW FINDING for ORCH to file (not covered by ISS-0811/0812/0813). User.status is declared uppercase but the wire emits lowercase. web/src/types/api.ts:435 declares status?: 'ACTIVE' | 'INACTIVE' and web/src/api/identity.ts:24 (usersApi.update) SENDS 'ACTIVE' | 'INACTIVE'. lib/letflow/identity/user.ex:41 is field(:status, Ecto.Enum, values: [:active, :inactive]) and user_map/1 (lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex:735) emits Atom.to_string(user.status) with no String.upcase anywhere in that router -- so the wire value is "active". Any user.status === 'ACTIVE' comparison in web/ is therefore always false, and the uppercase value usersApi.update sends may not validate. This is a live value-domain mismatch, not only a type lie. Out of scope here (User/usersApi is ISS-0812's surface). Suggested scope for the issue: 'every read and write of User.status in web/src/'.

NEW FINDING for ORCH to file. User.roles and User.created_at are declared REQUIRED at web/src/types/api.ts:437,441, but user_map/1 (lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex:729-740) emits neither -- it emits inserted_at/updated_at and no roles at all. Affects every usersApi consumer. Same class as ISS-0811 but a different type and a different mapper, so not a duplicate. This is why the design introduces GroupMember rather than reusing User for group members.

NEW FINDING for ORCH to file. CursorPage<T> (web/src/types/api.ts:14-18) declares has_more: boolean, which Letflow.Api.Pagination.Page never emits -- its @derive list (lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex:81) is [:items, :next_cursor, :count]. CursorPage<T> is used by ~12 call sites across web/src/api/ (audit, definitions, dlq, instances, modules, promotions, services, tasks). Whether every one of those routes actually uses Pagination.Page was NOT established in this step -- the finding is that it needs its own audit, not that all 12 are wrong. This is why the design adds GroupMemberPage rather than reusing CursorPage.

NEW FINDING for ORCH to file. The group-members dialog shows at most the first 50 members (Pagination.default_page_size/0, lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex:99) and next_cursor is returned but unread. Pre-existing behaviour that this fix makes reachable for the first time rather than behaviour the fix introduces; paging the dialog is UI work with no acceptance criterion in this run. See the design's OQ-2.

result.next_action: Re-route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for rework iteration 1 re-gate. The two blocking/rework findings F-1 and F-2 are addressed in design sections 7, 7.1, 8 and the new path-convention table in section 1; no decision (a)-(d) changed.

findings.validator_statement: Row 8 T-0765-MEMBERS-SHAPE cannot fail pre-fix. The mandated ISS-0736 harness installs a window.fetch spy whose Response the test itself defines, so no URL is dialled and there is no 404. client.ts:158-169 returns response.json() verbatim, and T is erased at runtime, so the pre-fix client.get<User[]> and the post-fix client.get<GroupMemberPage> behave identically on the same spy body. The row PASSES under npm test pre-fix, and the section summary "rows 1-11, each of which fails against the pre-fix commit" was false as written.
findings.resolution: ACCEPTED IN FULL -- the error was CODE-DESIGNER's, not TEST-DESIGNER's to discover. Option taken: FOLD, not re-classify. Old rows 7 (T-0765-MEMBERS-PATH) and 8 (T-0765-MEMBERS-SHAPE) are merged into a single row 7, T-0765-MEMBERS, whose one `it` block carries both a path half (i) and the no-unwrap half (ii). Half (i) fails pre-fix on the /api/v1/admin/ literal, so the row genuinely goes red. Half (ii) is explicitly re-classified in the design as a FORWARD REGRESSION GUARD against a future .items unwrap -- INV-B's guard -- and is stated NOT to be fail-first evidence. Rows 9-12 renumber to 8-11; every cross-reference in the AC map (section 8) was updated.
findings.what_now_carries_decision_b_fail_first: A new section 7.1 states plainly that NO runtime row can, because request<T> is a verbatim pass-through and T is erased at runtime -- so a type-only change has no runtime failure to demonstrate. WF-03 Step 4's "when the pre-fix failure is non-existence, mutate" clause is applied by analogy, and the mutants are specified in the design rather than left to TEST-DESIGNER: M-1a keeps the retype and reverts ONLY the six GroupsPage.tsx edits, then runs npm run type-check and must produce tsc errors at GroupsPage.tsx :103/:223/:227/:228 (and npm test must still pass under it -- that is the point: it shows the runtime suite is blind to the retype while type-check is not). M-1b is the opposite-direction control: revert the retype to client.get<User[]> while keeping the GroupsPage edits, and tsc must error on membersPage?.items over User[]. WF-03 Step 4's revert-and-verify discipline is restated as binding (throwaway worktree, or git checkout -- plus a quoted-empty git status --porcelain web/ and a green re-run).
findings.section_summary_corrected: The false sentence is gone. Section 7.1 replaces it with an explicit two-column table: FAILS pre-fix = rows 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7(i), 8, 9, 10; PASSES pre-fix (enumeration / forward guard, never red either way) = rows 7(ii) and 11.

findings.validator_statement: Sections 1.3, 2, 3.1 and 4 used a bare `identity.ex` for the ROUTER while section 1.2 used it for the CONTEXT. Following section 4's "identity.ex:483-489" literally lands in lib/letflow/identity.ex, where those lines are unrelated moduledoc prose; the real target is lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex.
findings.resolution: ACCEPTED IN FULL. A binding "Path convention" table was added at the head of section 1 naming all three identity files (router / context / API client) and stating that no bare identity.ex appears, with the 483-489 collision cited as the concrete reason. Every previously-bare citation was rewritten to lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex:NNN (:227-229, :468-472, :525-537, :483-489, :729-740, :735, :749-757, :829-831). Section 1.3's table, whose rows used bare :NNN, now carries an explicit footnote that every bare :NNN in it is a line in lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex, and its last row gained the previously-missing (:588).

findings.validator_statement: The routers/identity.ex:483-489 comment's own premise -- "no existing Letflow caller depends on the array shape either way" -- is already stale, since GroupsPage.tsx:76 passes [userId] today. Decision (c) makes that comment true rather than contradicting it.
findings.resolution: Folded into section 4 as a "Note for a later reader": decision (c) does not contradict the recorded backend decision, it restores the comment's premise by removing the one caller that had drifted from it. Costs one paragraph and forestalls a re-litigation.

findings.validator_statement: OQ-1 resolved CODE-DESIGNER's way: the ISS-0811 carve-out wins, Group stays untouched. No rework to section 3.1 or section 5 on that ground.
findings.resolution: No change required. OQ-1 is left in the design as the record of how the scope overlap was resolved and by whom.

rework_history.sections_confirmed_unchanged_by_the_gate: Sections 1-6, 8 and 9 survived the validator's independent re-derivation, and decisions (a)-(d) all stand on verified premises: frontend_developer_guide.md:83-88 confirmed verbatim, resolve_member_user_id/1's two clauses confirmed at lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex:525-531, the zero-callers grep reproduced, and the source-scan.spec.ts `fetch(` constraint confirmed real and whole-file. No decision was revisited in this rework.
rework_history.downstream_issue_filed_from_this_step: The section 11 User.status finding is now ISS-0814 (queue 814, GH #1802), verified against source by ORCH.
